newsitem.title: USA: Knoxville, Tenn., plans new convention center.
newsitem.headline: Knoxville, Tenn., plans new convention center.

text.p: The $197.8 million fiscal 1998 budget for Knoxville, Tenn., includes $3.5 million for design work on a proposed new convention center, city officials said Thursday.
"We're falling behind cities of our size in attracting large conventions because of not having the facilities available," city Spokesman Charlie Barker said.
He said the center would boost downtown business and create 1,000 new jobs.
Funding has not been pinned down. The city is considering a public-private partnership, with the public portion to be financed with general obligation bonds.
The city has a 14-year-old convention center but it "is very small and very limited in what can go into it," Barker said.
City officials plan public hearings on the project in September, with construction to begin within two years.
